qualification.reason: The document is a Request for Proposals (RFP) issued by the City of Providence Board of Contract and Supply for the Hope High School Boiler Demolition and Abatement project. It includes a detailed scope of work, submission instructions, deadlines, pre-bid conference, and bid requirements, clearly indicating a procurement solicitation.

quotes.quote: REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS
Item Description:  Hope High School- Boiler Demolition and Abatement
Complete responses must be received by Monday, July 27, 2026, at 2:15 pm

The City   of   Providence   is   seeking   comprehensive,   competitive   proposals   from   licensed   and   qualified   
environmental and demolition contractors. The objective is to safely and legally perform the hazardous materials 
abatement and selective demolition/removal of the existing boiler systems at Hope High School located at 324 
Hope Street, Providence, RI 02906.

findings.title: Out-of-State Corporation Registration
findings.fact: Out-of-state corporations must qualify or register to transact business in Rhode Island.

quotes.quote: A bidder who is an out-of-state corporation shall qualify or register to transact business in this State, in accordance with the Rhode Island Business Corporation Act, RIGL Sec. 7-1.2-1401, et seq.

findings.title: Certificate of Good Standing Required
findings.fact: The successful bidder must provide a Certificate of Good Standing with the Rhode Island Secretary of State.

quotes.quote: Certificate of Good Standing with the Rhode Island Secretary of State.

findings.title: Apprentice Requirements
findings.fact: Construction projects valued at $100,000 or more must utilize not less than 15% of total hours worked by apprentices.

quotes.quote: This ordinance outlines requirements for utilizing not less than 15% of total hours worked by apprentices.

findings.title: First Source Requirements
findings.fact: The project is subject to First Source Agreements requiring hiring of Providence residents.

quotes.quote: This ordinance outlines requirements for hiring Providence residents to work on this project.

findings.title: Proof of Insurance Required
findings.fact: The successful bidder must provide proof of insurance.

quotes.quote: Proof of Insurance.

findings.title: Business Tax ID Required
findings.fact: The successful bidder must provide a Business Tax ID after award.

quotes.quote: Business Tax ID will be requested after an award is approved by the Board of Contract and Supply.

findings.title: Bid Validity Period
findings.fact: Awards will be made within 90 days of bid opening, and bid prices must remain firm during this period.

quotes.quote: Awards will be made within nighty (90) days of bid opening. All bid prices will be considered firm, unless qualified otherwise.

findings.title: Earnest Money Deposit (EMD) Submission
findings.fact: No specific EMD amount or form is specified; the bid terms indicate that financial assurances may be required, but the checkboxes are not marked. The document states 'No financial assurance is necessary for this item.'

quotes.quote: No financial assurance is necessary for this item.

findings.title: Cash discounts not considered in determining lowest responsible bidder
findings.fact: In determining the lowest responsible bidder, cash discounts based on preferable payment terms will not be considered.

quotes.quote: In determining the lowest responsible bidder, cash discounts based on preferable payment terms will not be considered.

findings.title: Equal prices may result in award to one bidder or split award
findings.fact: Where prices are the same, the Board of Contract and Supply reserves the right to award to one bidder, or to split the award.

quotes.quote: Where prices are the same, the Board of Contract and Supply reserves the right to award to one bidder, or to split the award.

findings.title: No Interest on Overdue Payments
findings.fact: The City shall not be obligated to pay interest on any overdue invoice or payment.

quotes.quote: In no circumstances shall the City be obligated to pay or shall you be entitled to receive interest on any overdue invoice or payment.

findings.title: MBE/WBE Reporting Deadline
findings.fact: The successful bidder shall report on applicable participation within ten (10) days after receipt of Notice of Award.

quotes.quote: The successful bidder shall report on applicable participation within ten (10) days after receipt of Notice of Award.

findings.title: No Interest on Overdue Payments
findings.fact: The City shall not be obligated to pay any costs associated with your collection of an outstanding invoice.

quotes.quote: In no circumstances shall the City be obligated to pay any costs associated with your collection of an outstanding invoice.

findings.title: Mandatory Pre-Bid Conference
findings.fact: A mandatory pre-bid conference is required for this project.
findings.business_implication: Attendance is mandatory; failure to attend will result in bid disqualification.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure a representative attends the pre-bid conference on June 30, 2026 at 4:00 PM at 324 Hope Street, Providence, RI 02906.

quotes.quote: There will be a Mandatory Pre-Bid Conference.

findings.title: Licensed and Qualified Contractors Required
findings.fact: The City is seeking proposals from licensed and qualified environmental and demolition contractors.
findings.business_implication: Only contractors with appropriate licenses and qualifications for environmental and demolition work are eligible to bid.
findings.action_recommendation: Verify that your company holds all required licenses and certifications for environmental and demolition work in Rhode Island.

quotes.quote: The City   of   Providence   is   seeking   comprehensive,   competitive   proposals   from   licensed   and   qualified   environmental and demolition contractors.

findings.title: MBE/WBE Participation Goal
findings.fact: There is a 20% MBE/WBE combined participation goal for this project.
findings.business_implication: Bidders must either meet the 20% MBE/WBE participation goal or submit a waiver request form to be considered for award.
findings.action_recommendation: Identify and engage certified MBE/WBE subcontractors or suppliers to meet the 20% goal, or prepare a waiver request form with documentation of good faith efforts.

quotes.quote: If you did not meet the 20% MBE/WBE combined participation goal, submit a Waiver Request Form.
I acknowledge the City of Providence’s goal of a combined MBE/WBE participation is 20% of the total bid value.

findings.title: MBE/WBE Certification Required
findings.fact: All MBE/WBE subcontractors/suppliers must be certified by the Office of Diversity, Equity and Opportunity at the time of bid.
findings.business_implication: Any MBE/WBE subcontractor or supplier used to meet the participation goal must be certified by the Office of Diversity, Equity and Opportunity at bid submission; otherwise, the bid may be considered non-responsive.
findings.action_recommendation: Verify that all MBE/WBE subcontractors/suppliers are certified by the Office of Diversity, Equity and Opportunity before bid submission.

quotes.quote: Please note that all MBE/WBE subcontractors/suppliers must be certified by the Office of Diversity, Equity and Opportunity at the time of bid.

findings.title: Final Bid Submission Deadline
findings.fact: Bids must be submitted by 2:15 P.M. on July 27, 2026, at the Department of the City Clerk, Room 311, City Hall, 25 Dorrance Street, Providence.
findings.business_implication: Bids must be received by the specified deadline; late bids will be rejected. The bid opening is at 2:15 P.M. on the same date.
findings.action_recommendation: Plan to submit the bid well before the deadline to avoid any last-minute issues. Ensure the bid is delivered to the correct address and includes the required number of copies.

quotes.quote: Bids may be submitted up to 2:15 P.M. on the above meeting date at the Department of the City Clerk. Room 311, City Hall. 25 Dorrance Street, Providence.
Complete responses must be received by Monday, July 27, 2026, at 2:15 pm and sent to the City Clerk (25 Dorrance Street Providence, RI 02903 Room 311).

findings.title: Pre-Bid Conference Date and Time
findings.fact: A mandatory pre-bid conference is scheduled for June 30, 2026, at 4:00 pm at 324 Hope Street, Providence, RI 02906.
findings.business_implication: Attendance is mandatory; failure to attend will result in bid disqualification. This is a critical deadline to plan for.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure a representative attends the pre-bid conference on June 30, 2026, at 4:00 pm at the specified location. Mark the date and prepare any questions in advance.

quotes.quote: There will be a Mandatory Pre-Bid Conference. Date of Pre-Bid Conference: 6/30/2026 Time: 4:00 pm
Pre-Bid Conference Tuesday June 30, 2026, at 4PM

findings.title: Portal Upload Instructions
findings.fact: No electronic submissions will be accepted; bids must be submitted in person to the City Clerk. The document states 'No faxed or electronic submissions will be accepted.'
findings.business_implication: Bids must be physically delivered to the City Clerk's office by the deadline. Electronic or faxed submissions will be rejected, so proper planning for physical delivery is essential.
findings.action_recommendation: Prepare a physical bid package and arrange for in-person delivery to the City Clerk's office (25 Dorrance Street, Providence, RI 02903, Room 311) before the deadline. Confirm the exact delivery location and hours.

quotes.quote: No faxed or electronic submissions will be accepted.

findings.title: Award to lowest qualified and responsible bidder
findings.fact: The Board of Contract and Supply will make the award to the lowest qualified and responsible bidder.
findings.business_implication: Price is a primary factor, but the bidder must also be deemed 'qualified and responsible.' This means the bidder must meet all technical and financial requirements and have a good track record.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure your bid is competitive on price while also demonstrating your qualifications, experience, and financial stability. Provide all required documentation to prove your responsibility.

quotes.quote: The Board of Contract and Supply will make the award to the lowest qualified and responsible bidder.

findings.title: Right to reject any and all bids
findings.fact: The Board of Contract and Supply reserves the right to reject any and all bids.
findings.business_implication: Even if you submit a compliant bid, the City may reject all bids if it deems it in its best interest. This introduces uncertainty, but it is a standard provision.
findings.action_recommendation: Do not assume that submitting a bid guarantees an award. Focus on submitting the most competitive and compliant bid possible, but be aware that the City may reject all bids.

quotes.quote: The Board of Contract and Supply reserves the right to reject any and all bids.

findings.title: Disqualification for failure to follow submission instructions
findings.fact: Failure to meet specified deadlines, follow specific submission instructions, or enclose all required documents with all applicable signatures will result in disqualification, or in an inability to appropriately evaluate bids.
findings.business_implication: Strict compliance with submission requirements is mandatory. Any deviation, such as missing signatures or incomplete forms, can lead to immediate disqualification.
findings.action_recommendation: Thoroughly review the bid package checklist and ensure all required forms are completed, signed, and included in the correct order. Double-check that all deadlines are met and that the submission is made in person as required.

quotes.quote: Failure to meet specified deadlines, follow specific submission instructions, or enclose all required documents with all applicable signatures will result in disqualification, or in an inability to appropriately evaluate bids.

findings.title: Disqualification for submitting sensitive information directly to issuing department
findings.fact: Bidders who attempt to submit sensitive information directly to the issuing department to protect pricing terms from becoming public will be disqualified.
findings.business_implication: Bidders must not attempt to bypass the official submission process by sending sensitive information directly to the issuing department, as this will result in automatic disqualification. This rule ensures transparency and equal treatment of all bidders.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure all required information, including any sensitive details, is submitted through the official channel (City Clerk's office) as part of the bid packet. Do not attempt to protect pricing terms by submitting them separately.

quotes.quote: Bidders who make such an attempt will be disqualified.

findings.title: Payment Terms: 60 Days
findings.fact: Invoices submitted to the City shall be payable sixty (60) days from the time of receipt by the City.
findings.business_implication: The City will take up to 60 days to pay invoices after receipt, which may impact cash flow. The payment clock starts only when the City receives the invoice with sufficient supporting documentation.
findings.action_recommendation: Plan cash flow accordingly, considering the 60-day payment term. Ensure invoices are complete and include all required documentation to avoid delays in payment processing.

quotes.quote: Invoices submitted to the City shall be payable sixty (60) days from the time of receipt by the City.

findings.title: Performance and Payment Bond Required
findings.fact: A performance and payment bond with a satisfactory surety company will be posted by the bidder in a sum equal to one hundred per centum (100%) of the awarded contract.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must secure a performance and payment bond for 100% of the contract value, which involves additional costs and requires a surety company. Failure to provide the bond may result in disqualification or contract award issues.
findings.action_recommendation: Arrange for a performance and payment bond from a satisfactory surety company in the amount of 100% of the contract value. Factor the bond premium into the bid price and ensure the surety is acceptable to the City.

quotes.quote: A performance and payment bond with a satisfactory surety company will be posted by the bidder in a sum equal to one hundred per centum (100%) of the awarded contract.

findings.title: Prevailing Wage Requirements
findings.fact: Any construction over $1,000.00 is required by state law to pay state prevailing wage.
findings.business_implication: For construction work exceeding $1,000, the bidder must pay state prevailing wages, which are typically higher than standard wages. This increases labor costs and requires compliance with state wage determinations.
findings.action_recommendation: Review the applicable prevailing wage rates for the project location and incorporate them into the bid. Ensure compliance with certified payroll requirements and maintain accurate records.

quotes.quote: Prevailing Wages: Any construction over $ 1,000.00 is required by state law to pay state prevailing wage.

findings.title: Payment Requisition Conditions
findings.fact: Compliance reporting for apprenticeship and First Source requirements is a condition for payment.
findings.business_implication: Payments will be withheld if the bidder fails to submit compliance reports for apprenticeship and First Source requirements. This adds administrative burden and potential cash flow risk if reporting is not timely.
findings.action_recommendation: Establish a process to track and report apprenticeship and First Source compliance. Submit required reports with each payment requisition to avoid delays. Attend mandatory meetings to understand reporting formats.

quotes.quote: The attention of prospective bidders is also called to the fact that reporting the efforts undertaken and progress towards achieving the requirements in this ordinance is a condition for payment.
The attention of prospective bidders is called to the fact that reporting the efforts undertaken and progress towards achieving the requirements in this ordinance is a condition for payment.

findings.title: Indemnification Obligation
findings.fact: Contractor must indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the City from all claims, damages, losses, etc. arising from the work.
findings.business_implication: The contractor assumes broad liability for any claims or damages arising from the work, including legal fees, which could be financially significant and not limited to the contract value.
findings.action_recommendation: Review insurance coverage to ensure it is adequate to cover potential indemnification obligations. Consider negotiating for a mutual indemnification clause or a cap on indemnification to the extent permitted by law.

quotes.quote: To the fullest extent permitted by law, you shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the City, its employees, officers, agents, and assigns from and against any and all claims, damages, losses, allegations, demands, actions, causes of action, suits, obligations, fines, penalties, judgments, liabilities, costs and expenses, including but not limited to attorneys’ fees, of any nature whatsoever arising out of, in connection with, or resulting from the performance of the work provided in the Agreement.

findings.title: Uncapped Liability
findings.fact: The City does not agree to limit contractor's liability to the contract price or any other monetary limit.
findings.business_implication: The contractor faces unlimited liability for any claims arising from the contract, which could expose the business to significant financial risk beyond the contract value.
findings.action_recommendation: Assess the potential risks and ensure adequate insurance coverage. Consider negotiating for a liability cap, such as limiting liability to the contract price or the amount of insurance proceeds, to mitigate exposure.

quotes.quote: The City shall not subject itself to any contractual limitations on liability. The City shall have the time permitted within the applicable statute of limitations, and no less, to bring or assert any and all causes of action, suits, claims or demands the City may have arising out of, in connection with, or resulting from the performance of the work provided in the Agreement, and in no event does the City agree to limit your liability to the price of the Agreement or any other monetary limit.

findings.title: Insurance Requirements
findings.fact: Contractor must maintain insurance coverage required by RFP or commercially reasonable, and name City as additional insured on general liability and umbrella policies.
findings.business_implication: The contractor must secure and maintain specific insurance coverage, including naming the City as an additional insured, which may increase insurance costs and administrative burden.
findings.action_recommendation: Obtain and maintain the required insurance policies, ensuring the City is named as an additional insured. Verify that coverage limits are adequate and review policies to confirm compliance with the contract requirements.

quotes.quote: You shall maintain throughout the term of this Agreement the insurance coverage that is required by the RFP or, if none is required in the RFP, insurance coverage that is considered in your industry to be commercially reasonable, and you agree to name the City as an additional insured on your general liability policy and on any umbrella policy you carry.

findings.title: Certificate of Insurance Required
findings.fact: A certificate of insurance will normally be required of a successful vendor.
findings.business_implication: The contractor must provide proof of insurance to the City, which is a standard requirement but adds an administrative step.
findings.action_recommendation: Prepare to provide a certificate of insurance upon award. Ensure the certificate is issued by the insurance carrier and lists the City as certificate holder.

quotes.quote: A certificate of insurance will normally be required of a successful vendor.

findings.title: Liquidated Damages for Bid Bond Default
findings.fact: If a bid bond is required, the amount shall be retained as liquidated damages in case of default.
findings.business_implication: If the contractor fails to sign and deliver the contract after being awarded, the bid bond amount will be forfeited as liquidated damages, representing a financial penalty.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure that the bid bond is in place and that the contractor is prepared to honor the contract award to avoid forfeiture. Understand the bond amount and conditions to mitigate risk.

quotes.quote: A bid bond in the amount of           per centum (%) of the proposed total price, must be deposited with the City Clerk as a guarantee that the contract will be signed and delivered by the bidder; and the amount of such bid bond shall be retained for the use of the City as liquidated damages in case of default.

findings.title: No Interest on Overdue Invoices
findings.fact: The City is not obligated to pay interest on overdue invoices or costs associated with collection.
findings.business_implication: The bidder will not receive any interest or collection cost recovery if the City pays late, which could impact cash flow and increase the cost of doing business.
findings.action_recommendation: Factor in the cost of delayed payments into pricing and ensure sufficient cash flow to cover potential late payments. Consider negotiating shorter payment terms or milestone payments.

quotes.quote: In no circumstances shall the City be obligated to pay or shall you be entitled to receive interest on any overdue invoice or payment. In no circumstances shall the City be obligated to pay any costs associated with your collection of an outstanding invoice.

findings.title: No Liability for Public Record Disclosure
findings.fact: The City bears no liability for sensitive information becoming public record if bidder encloses it.
findings.business_implication: If the bidder includes sensitive information in the bid packet, it may become public record, and the City will not be liable for any resulting disclosure, potentially exposing the bidder to competitive or privacy risks.
findings.action_recommendation: Carefully review the RFP to identify what information is required and only submit sensitive information when explicitly requested. If sensitive information must be submitted, consider redacting it or seeking confidential treatment, but be aware of the City's policy.

quotes.quote: If sensitive information that has not been requested is enclosed or if a bidder opts to enclose the defined supplemental information prior to the issuing department’s request in the bidding packet submitted to the City Clerk, the City of Providence has no obligation to redact those details and bears no liability associated with the information becoming public record.

findings.title: Independent Contractor Status
findings.fact: Contractor is an independent contractor and not an employee or agent of the City, thus responsible for own taxes and benefits.
findings.business_implication: The bidder will not receive employee benefits and must handle all tax withholdings and contributions, which could increase administrative burden and costs.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure that the bidder's pricing accounts for self-employment taxes and benefits. Verify that the bidder has appropriate insurance and tax arrangements in place.

quotes.quote: You are an independent contractor and in no way does this Agreement render you an employee or agent of the City or entitle you to fringe benefits, workers’ compensation, pension obligations, retirement or any other employment benefits. The City shall not deduct federal or state income taxes, social security or Medicare withholdings, or any other taxes required to be deducted by an employer, and this is your responsibility to yourself and your employees and agents.

findings.title: No Assignment Without Consent
findings.fact: Contractor shall not assign rights or obligations without prior written consent of the City; unauthorized assignment is voidable.
findings.business_implication: The bidder cannot transfer the contract to another entity without the City's consent, which could limit flexibility in corporate restructuring or subcontracting arrangements.
findings.action_recommendation: If the bidder anticipates any assignment or change of control, seek the City's written consent in advance. Ensure that any subcontracting does not constitute an assignment.

quotes.quote: You shall not assign your rights and obligations under this Agreement without the prior written consent of the City. Any assignment without prior written consent of the City shall be voidable at the election of the City.

findings.title: No Waiver of Future Breaches
findings.fact: Failure of City to require performance does not waive future rights, and waiver of one breach does not waive subsequent breaches.
findings.business_implication: The City's failure to enforce a provision or its acceptance of a breach does not prevent it from enforcing the contract later, so the bidder cannot rely on past leniency.
findings.action_recommendation: The bidder should consistently comply with all contract terms and not assume that the City's inaction constitutes a waiver. Document any instances where the City may have waived a requirement to protect against future claims.

quotes.quote: The failure of the City to require performance of any provision shall not affect the City’s right to require performance at any time thereafter, nor shall a waiver of any breach or default of this Agreement constitute a waiver of any subsequent breach or default or a waiver of the provision itself.

findings.title: Governing Law and Jurisdiction
findings.fact: Agreement governed by Rhode Island law; contractor submits to jurisdiction in Rhode Island.
findings.business_implication: The contractor must be prepared to resolve any disputes in Rhode Island courts, which may increase legal costs and inconvenience if the contractor is not located in Rhode Island.
findings.action_recommendation: Assess the feasibility of litigating in Rhode Island and consider whether to negotiate for a more favorable venue or ensure local counsel is available.

quotes.quote: The Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Rhode Island. You expressly submit yourself to and agree that any and all actions arising out of, in connection with, or resulting from the performance of the Agreement or relationship between the parties shall occur solely in the venue and jurisdiction of the State of Rhode Island or the federal court located in Rhode Island.

findings.title: Post-Termination Compensation
findings.fact: In the event of termination by the City, the contractor is entitled to just and equitable compensation for satisfactory work completed and expenses incurred up to the date of termination.
findings.business_implication: The contractor has some financial protection if the City terminates the contract, but the amount is not predetermined and may be subject to negotiation or dispute.
findings.action_recommendation: Document all work and expenses meticulously to support a claim for compensation in case of termination, and consider negotiating a more specific formula for compensation.

quotes.quote: In the event of termination by the City, you shall be entitled to just and equitable compensation for any satisfactory work completed and expenses incurred up to the date of termination.

findings.title: Force Majeure Conditions
findings.fact: Deliveries and/or completion are subject to strikes, lockouts, accidents, and Acts of God, which may excuse performance.
findings.business_implication: The contractor may be excused from performance delays or failures caused by events beyond its control, but the scope is limited to the listed events and may not cover all unforeseen circumstances.
findings.action_recommendation: Review the force majeure clause to ensure it covers relevant risks and consider negotiating broader language to include pandemics, government actions, or supply chain disruptions.

quotes.quote: It is agreed that deliveries and/or completion are subject to strikes, lockouts, accidents, and Acts of God.
